## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Putta Sutta* (Iti 74; PTS It 62) is a short discourse in the *Itivuttaka* (section It 3.25) addressing the classification of children. The Buddha delineates three types of sons and daughters in comparison to their parents: those of superior or heightened birth (*atijāta*), those of equal or similar birth (*anujāta*), and those of inferior or lowered birth (*avajāta*), defining these distinctions through ethical and spiritual behavior rather than caste or biological lineage.

The references located in the provided secondary corpus represent false positives for other texts sharing the component *-puttasutta* (such as the *Kesaputta Sutta*, *Sāriputta Sutta*, *Māluṅkyaputta Sutta*, and *Cunda Kammāraputta Sutta*), and the sutta itself receives no sustained analysis in those excerpts.
